m3-t1.question: In simple terms, how does a diffusion image model generate a picture?
options: It searches the internet for a matching photo
It starts from random noise and removes it step by step, steering toward the prompt
It copies and pastes parts of training images
It draws vector shapes from rules
m3-t1.explanation: Diffusion models are trained to reverse noise; generation starts from static and denoises toward the caption you supply.

m3-t1.question: Why is text inside generated images often wrong?
options: Models are not allowed to write
Letters are strict shapes that the model learned only as fuzzy visual patterns
Images have no colour channel for text
m3-t1.explanation: The model learned letters as patterns, not rules. Newer tools improve, but adding text in a design tool is usually smarter.

m3-t1.question: Which tool type is the recommended default for everyday generation in this course?
options: Chat assistants or design-suite AI, escalating to dedicated tools only when needed
m3-t1.explanation: Generate in a chat assistant or design suite, refine in a design tool, escalate only for demanding briefs.

m3-t1.question: What should you write BEFORE prompting an image tool?
options: A brief: purpose, audience, format, must-haves, style, constraints
m3-t1.explanation: A five-minute brief saves dozens of wasted generations.

m3-t1.question: Which is a correct licence rule from the lesson?
options: All AI images are public domain
Free tiers always allow commercial use
Read the tool's terms; prefer licensed-data tools for client work; never real faces or trademarked characters
m3-t1.explanation: Ownership and commercial rights depend on tool terms and national law; keep records and be conservative for client work.

m3-t2.question: What is the recommended order of the image prompt formula?
options: Subject – Setting – Style – Composition – Lighting – Quality/Constraints
m3-t2.explanation: Models weigh early words more, so the subject leads and constraints close.

m3-t2.question: Why does the lesson advise against 'in the style of [living artist]'?
options: It is ethically dubious and often blocked; describe the qualities instead
m3-t2.explanation: Describe the properties you want (bold outlines, limited palette) rather than appropriating a living artist's style.

m3-t2.question: What is the fastest route to visual consistency across a set?
options: Generate each image with a new prompt
A reused base prompt plus reference images, changing only the subject
Using a different tool for each image
m3-t2.explanation: Lock style, palette, lighting and composition in a base prompt; vary only the subject.

m3-t2.question: You need a square image to become a 9:16 story without cropping the subject. Which edit?
m3-t2.explanation: Outpainting extends the canvas; the model fills the new area.

m3-t2.question: Which prompt best counters default bias for an Indian audience?
options: 'A diverse group of Indian college students in a Bengaluru campus'
m3-t2.explanation: Model defaults are not neutral; specify age, gender, region and attire deliberately.

m3-t3.question: Where should text be added for a poster?
options: In the design tool's text layer, with every letter checked
Never; posters should not have text
m3-t3.explanation: The design layer renders text perfectly and keeps it editable and translatable.

m3-t3.question: What is the first step in getting a good deck from an AI presentation tool?
options: Upload the raw report and accept the output
Write a sentence-title story first (one message per slide), then generate from that outline
m3-t3.explanation: A narrative outline with message titles produces a coherent deck; raw documents produce bullet dumps.

m3-t3.question: Why must charts never be drawn by an image generator?
options: The bars represent data that does not exist
m3-t3.explanation: A chart is a claim about numbers; build it from real data in a chart tool.

m3-t3.question: Which set is the five design fundamentals from the lesson?
m3-t3.explanation: These five fix most amateur designs; check them before exporting.

m3-t3.question: Which fonts are recommended when a design must render Kannada or Hindi correctly?
m3-t3.explanation: Noto fonts are free and cover Indian scripts reliably; still proofread with a native reader.

m3-t4.question: Which family of tools does 70% of the actual video work happen in?
m3-t4.explanation: Clips and avatars are raw material; the editor turns them into a finished video.

m3-t4.question: Why does the lesson prefer image-to-video over text-to-video?
options: Consistency and control improve greatly when you animate a still you already approved
m3-t4.explanation: Approving the still first removes most of the randomness.

m3-t4.question: Which is a non-negotiable rule for avatar videos?
options: Consent for any likeness used, and disclosure that the presenter is an AI avatar
m3-t4.explanation: Consent and disclosure protect people and viewers; both are required.

m3-t4.question: What should you do with auto-generated captions?
options: Proofread every word, especially names, numbers and Indian-language text
m3-t4.explanation: Most social video is watched muted; wrong captions are wrong content.

m3-t4.question: A 45-second spoken script is roughly how many words?
m3-t4.explanation: Speech runs at about 2–3 words per second; 30–60 seconds is 75–150 words.

m3-t5.question: What is a repurposing matrix?
options: A map from one core asset to many derived formats, each with a brief
m3-t5.explanation: Start from one strong asset and plan clips, cards, carousels, posts, posters and more.

m3-t5.question: Which three tools keep a brand consistent at scale?
options: Kit, base prompts, a pre-publish checklist
m3-t5.explanation: The kit fixes visuals, base prompts fix style and voice, and the checklist catches slips.

m3-t5.question: What minimum contrast ratio does the lesson give for text?
m3-t5.explanation: 4.5:1 is the widely used accessibility threshold for body text.

m3-t5.question: When must a synthetic image or video be labelled?
options: Whenever a reasonable viewer might believe it depicts a real person, place or event
Only if it is over one minute
m3-t5.explanation: Realistic depictions require labels; decorative imagery benefits from a brief note.

m3-t5.question: Which is one of the four pre-publish ethics questions?
options: Whose likeness, work or symbol appears — and do I have consent or rights?
Is the file size under 5 MB?
m3-t5.explanation: The four questions: mistaken for real? whose likeness/work? accurate and respectful? provable claims?
